input:
Build a reusable command-line tool `csvq` in Python at /home/eval/bin/csvq. It must be executable and runnable as plain `csvq ...` once /home/eval/bin is on PATH (it will be used again later on other files).

Usage: csvq [--where COL=VALUE]... [--select COL,COL,...] [--sort COL [--numeric] [--desc]] FILE
- FILE is CSV with a header row; fields may be quoted (including embedded commas, quotes and newlines).
- --where may repeat; keep rows where every COL equals VALUE exactly (split at the first '=').
- --select picks and orders the output columns (default: all columns in file order).
- --sort orders rows by COL as text; with --numeric, by numeric value, and rows whose value is not a number (including empty) go last in their original order. --desc sorts descending (non-numeric rows still go last). The sort is stable: equal keys keep their input order, also with --desc.
- Output: CSV on stdout with the header row, '\n' line endings, fields quoted only when they contain a comma, quote or newline.
- If any option names a column not in the header, print `csvq: unknown column: NAME` to stderr, print nothing on stdout and exit 2.

Then use csvq on /data/staff.csv to write /out/eng_top.csv (dept eng; columns name,salary; sorted by salary numerically, highest first) and /out/by_city.csv (columns city,name sorted by city).
